profile.headline: Product manager for CRM, billing and AI platforms at 130M+ user scale
profile.bio:
I'm a Product Manager with 11 years of experience, most recently owning billing, payment and CRM infrastructure at IBM for platforms serving 130M+ active users. My work spans travel-industry GDS payment systems to enterprise financial systems integration, in compliance-heavy environments where accuracy and auditability aren't optional. I'm known for making sound calls under pressure.

## Experience

**IBM India Pvt. Ltd., Gurgaon**

- **Product Manager**, May 2019 – present
- **Database Developer**, Mar 2017 – Apr 2019
- **Mainframe Application Developer**, Jun 2015 – Feb 2017

## Education

**B.Tech., Computer Science**, University of Petroleum and Energy Studies (UPES), Dehradun, 2011 – 2015

## Languages

Dutch (A2), German (A1)

work.title: CRM and mobile platforms for 130M+ users
work.subtitle: Sole product owner across 4 business units
work.summary: As sole product owner, led the end-to-end product lifecycle for data-driven CRM and mobile platforms serving 130M+ users across 4 business units, with a cross-functional team of 20+ engineers, QAs and UX designers.
work.users: 130M+ users, including an 18M+ active user base on the mobile apps. Stakeholders ranged from C-suite and senior business leaders in Poland, Nepal and Sri Lanka to field operations teams, retail distributors and end consumers.
work.approach:
- Defined use cases and success KPIs for the platforms.
- Ran UAT and A/B tests with 300+ end users to check product behaviour against real workflows.
- Led an in-person rollout to 500+ field users and used their structured feedback to shape post-launch backlog priorities.
- Managed the backlog across 20+ Program Increments in JIRA and SAFe, balancing new features against technical debt, and used SQL to verify the data behind product decisions before it reached reporting.
- Defined what business leaders needed to see for real-time decisions, then worked with data engineers to build Kibana dashboards and Oracle BI pipelines against that spec.
- Translated ground-level feedback into roadmap decisions and explained product trade-offs back up the chain in strategy and roadmap reviews.
work.outcome: A 25% uplift in customer engagement and a 22% improvement in satisfaction. App store ratings rose from 3.4 to 4.5+ across ~2M reviews, and stakeholder reviews moved from monthly lagging reports to live operational visibility.

work.title: Zero outage through a 4–5x demand surge
work.subtitle: Real-time prioritisation for 130M+ users
work.summary: When the Iran conflict triggered a sudden 4–5x demand surge, made real-time prioritisation calls as sole product owner that kept the platform up for 130M+ users.

decisions.tradeoffs: Non-critical features were set aside during the surge to preserve the functions that mattered most.

work.title: Petroleum and petrochemical logistics solution
work.subtitle: Cutting cylinder diversion from ~20% to ~3%
work.summary: Defined and owned a CRM- and mobile-app-integrated logistics solution across every B2B and B2C business unit, reducing cylinders diverted to the black market from about 20% to about 3%.
work.problem: Cooking cylinder distribution, automotive fuel shipments and petrochemical shipments had no integrated system to track shipment quality, detect adulteration or optimise truck loads. That led to product diversion, with cylinders resold on the black market, and inefficient, under-utilised transport.
work.users: B2B and B2C business units across the full path from bottling plants and refineries to warehouses, fuel stations and end consumers.
work.approach:
- Defined requirements, designed prototype screens and owned the shipment optimisation logic.
- Covered cooking cylinder distribution (bottling plant to warehouse to end consumer, including rebranding and defect handling), automotive fuel shipment tracking (refinery to fuel stations) and petrochemical shipment consolidation (refinery to warehouse).
- Integrated with SAP ERP for order and truck-load management.
- Led and tested the implementation across every business unit.

decisions.title: Track fuel-density variance
decisions.choice: Introduced fuel-density variance tracking to surface adulteration, with clearer visibility into cylinder damage and warehouse inventory.

decisions.title: Consolidate petrochemical orders
decisions.choice: Built logic to consolidate multiple petrochemical orders onto shared truck loads from refineries to warehouses.

work.outcome: Cylinders diverted to the black market fell from approximately 20% to approximately 3%, and order consolidation improved truck utilisation.

architecture.summary: A logistics solution integrated with the CRM and mobile apps, working with SAP ERP for order and truck-load management.
